name: Question 11
problem: Consider the points $D(t,5,3)$, $E({t}^{2},2,t)$ and $F(t+3,{t}^{2},1).$ Find $∠EDF$ given that $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=6.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $D$, $E$, $F$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}d=⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩,\,e=⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩,\,f=⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△DEF$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠EDF=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040103/assets/c9cfb3e84e6f76d243125f2a09246b2a1300a0134e71359bb2b528082f064f93.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =e-d \\  & =⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,-3,\,t-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =f-d \\  & =⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,{t}^{2}-5,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=6$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF} & =6 \\ ({t}^{2}-t)\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot ({t}^{2}-5)+(t-3)\cdot (-2) & =6 \\ 3{t}^{2}-3t-3{t}^{2}+15-2t+6 & =6 \\ -5t+21 & =6 \\ -5t & =-15 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =⟨{3}^{2}-3,-3,3-3⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-3,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =⟨3,{3}^{2}-5,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}}{|\overset{\to }{DE}||\overset{\to }{DF}|} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{3\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{29}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}})≈{80.44}^{∘}.
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the points D(t,5,3), E(t2,2,t) and F(t+3,t2,1). Find ∠EDF given that DE→⋅DF→=6. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

a
70.99∘
b
75.22∘
c
85.33∘
d
78.55∘
e
80.44∘
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points D, E, F are

d=⟨t,5,3⟩,e=⟨t2,2,t⟩,f=⟨t+3,t2,1⟩.

The triangle △DEF is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠EDF=θ.

First, we find the components of DE→ and DF→: DE→=e−d=⟨t2,2,t⟩−⟨t,5,3⟩=⟨t2−t,−3,t−3⟩DF→=f−d=⟨t+3,t2,1⟩−⟨t,5,3⟩=⟨3,t2−5,−2⟩

Now, since DE→⋅DF→=6, we can solve for t, as follows:

DE→⋅DF→=6(t2−t)⋅3+(−3)⋅(t2−5)+(t−3)⋅(−2)=63t2−3t−3t2+15−2t+6=6−5t+21=6−5t=−15t=3

So, DE→=⟨32−3,−3,3−3⟩=⟨6,−3,0⟩,DF→=⟨3,32−5,−2⟩=⟨3,4,−2⟩.

Next, the cosine of the angle between DE→ and DF→ is

cos⁡θ=DE→⋅DF→|DE→||DF→|=662+(−3)2+0232+42+(−2)2=635⋅29=2145.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(2145)≈80.44∘.
